content:
**Reviewer-protocol audit: Sec.13 ad-hoc fallback + M3 decision debt (issues #535/#551)**

AUDIT FINDING (issue #572), zero-context summary. Full detail: docs/inbox/AGENT-REVIEW-HANDOFF.md.

FINDING 1 -- Sec.13 was being violated, and the entrypoint already exists.
brain/core/methodology/reviewer-protocol.md:364-380 (Sec.13) requires review subagents to be strict command executors of `npm run brain:review -- --pr <id>` (or `--issue <id> --mode ruling`), never given ad-hoc manual prompts. Across issues #535 and #551, every review instead ran through a generic dual-blind adversarial skill with hand-written prompts. The entrypoint is wired (package.json:64-66 -> brain/scripts/review/cli.mjs, ~28 tested modules) plus read-only `brain:review:queue` / `brain:review:board`.

The ad-hoc path did not lose defect-finding power (it found 6 real vacuous-pass routes in T7b, each proven by live mutation). It lost procedural rigour: reproducibility (no headRefOid binding, no rev counter), verified identity (identity.mjs fail-closed on same-login, #413 -- ad-hoc judges have none), an auditable brain-review/N YAML record (poster.mjs:155, readable by brain:review:queue / board.mjs / parse-verdict.mjs -- chat findings are invisible to all of it), the findings contract (verdict.mjs drops findings without `evidence:`, downgrades blockers without `cites:` to `correction`), and bounded escalation (evaluators/ruling.mjs always escalates a well-formed `## FORK`; rev >= 3 forces STOP).

RULE FOR AGENTS: when asked to review a brain PR or issue, run `npm run brain:review -- --pr <id>` (or `--issue <id> --mode ruling`) per Sec.13. If a reviewer identity (BRAIN_REVIEWER_TOKEN, cross-checked against reviewer.handle in brain.config.json) is not available, SAY SO EXPLICITLY and stop -- never silently substitute an ad-hoc chat review.

COMPLEMENTARITY: the dual-blind adversarial skill is a good FINDINGS PRODUCER, not a verdict. Feed its live mutations into the `evidence:` field and its doctrine citations into `cites:` -- a mutation stops being a chat artifact and becomes contracted evidence. brain-review/2 alone would not have found the six T7b routes; it is a verdict machine with evidence discipline, not a bug hunter.

HONEST SYMMETRY: on the adversarial axis the real protocol is currently no better. The refuter (evaluators/refuter.mjs) only runs when evidence_class: 'inferential', and no evaluator produces that value yet -- causal-admission.mjs:28 calls it "a no-op today".

FINDING 2 -- the missing 20% of M3 is decision debt, not implementation debt. /1 is complete and invocable; all four open gaps are blocked on a human ruling, not code (#124 restricts rulings to the maintainer):
- #284 refuter role -- two open FORKs (lazy vs always-on trigger; own brain-refute/1 block vs per-finding refuter: field).
- #477 a corrupt findings list parses as no findings -- parseJsonScalar returns null on unparseable input and parseVerdict drops it; unparseable and absent are indistinguishable. Mirrors the Sec.10 "never APPROVE on uncomputable evidence" rule, inverted, in the reader that feeds the evaluators.
- #483 validateSchemaV2 is inert -- exported, tested, zero production call sites; buildVerdict routes on causal_disposition unvalidated. A typo'd disposition or invented evidence_class reaches the posted verdict unchallenged.
- #495 parseBudgetClaim can fabricate a blocker -- scans the whole doc, accepts any N/M where M is a declared budget; 4 ordinary sentences (one verbatim from this repo's own test file) each produce a drift:counted-lines-budget blocker with an invented evidence: claim.
Also: #408 CLOSED, narrow producer only (pre-existing for local-checks; base-only stays unproducible by design). #442 CLOSED and shipped (brain.config.json:37-41 dogfoods brain-review/2 at tier lite). #569 (priority:high) is the structural fix for the T7b lineage -- a runtime getVcs spy replacing the text-shape scan.

OPERATIONAL LESSONS (cost real time, worth repeating): verify a mutation actually landed before trusting a red (#409); give each adversarial reviewer its own worktree -- git stash is repository-scoped, not per-worktree; `gh issue view --json` / `gh issue edit --add-label` use GraphQL and fail under GraphQL rate limiting while `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/...` (REST) stays healthy; six routes into one T7b defect across four rounds -- widening a text scanner buys one shape and gives away the next, change the mechanism once the count repeats.
